entries.lesson_title: Using Derivatives to Transform Piecewise Linear Signals
entries.lesson_core_move: Transform a piecewise linear signal by differentiating it into simpler step and impulse terms, applying Laplace derivative properties, and solving algebraically for $X(s)$.

images.section_title: Introduction to Using Derivatives to Transform Piecewise Linear Signals
images.image_description: A compact figure with three time-domain sketches: causal ramp, shifted ramp, and finite ramp ending at a breakpoint. Mark slope regions, kink/endpoints, and map each region to derivative support types: constant step segments and vertical impulses.
images.report: One compact figure with three aligned examples: causal ramp, shifted ramp, and finite ramp ending at a breakpoint.; Top row shows the piecewise-linear signals; bottom row shows the derivative support as step segments and an endpoint impulse.; Shared breakpoint guides keep the signal and derivative panels visually aligned across the three examples.
